scientific_hypothesis: Germanium (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) form a viable material pair for mid-IR dual-band bandpass filters on CaF2 substrate, achieving high transmission in 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm bands while blocking 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm, with 22 total layers in a dual-cavity topology.
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has documented mid-IR transparency unlike Si/SiO2
Higher index contrast than Si/SiO2 enables sharper band edges
22 layers provides sufficient blocking while staying under 24-layer limit
known_risks: Ge may exhibit absorption features in mid-IR requiring verification
Thermal stress between Ge and ZnS during deposition
Cavity coupling may produce unwanted spectral ripple
expected_observations: best_target_score should exceed or match route_01's 0.955 if initialization improves convergence
tightest_margin should not decrease relative to route_01 candidates
valid_candidates count should remain similar to route_01's 9 if constraints are equally feasible
If hypothesis is false: best_target_score will stagnate below 0.955 despite constrained initialization
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to route_01 historical best (0.955) is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge initialization benefit as negligible -> stop and retain route_01 topology
If valid_candidates = 0, judge initialization constraints as infeasible -> relax thickness bounds to [30, 200] nm and re-run
